messages:
noah_pm: Quick follow-up from today's all-hands: can someone confirm the release cadence we should plan for next quarter, and what's the explicit oncall expectation during canary windows? Also what's the minimum test/quality bar to start a canary?

tara_eng: Short answer: monthly feature releases (targeting week 1), with a 10-14 day feature-freeze window. Patches/hotfixes pushed as needed via fast-path.

raj_sre: Canary owner expectation: the person named in the rollout PR as canary_owner is the primary responder for the canary window and must post a kickoff in #eng-oncall. If SLA-monitored routes are affected, escalate to SRE lead before >20% traffic.

elaine_cto: Canary duration is risk-dependent (typical 12-72h). Promote to full once the agreed metric window is stable. For high-risk infra changes we require multiple canary cohorts.

noah_pm: what exact metrics do we gate on?

tara_eng: Primary gates: P95 latency <= 1.2x baseline, error-rate delta < 0.1% absolute on service errors, and zero customer-facing regressions in smoke jobs. CI smoke/regression must be green. Also check model quality regressions for any inference-facing change (compare eval set).

devrel: Is there a freeze checklist engineers can reference? A lot of folks ask which items are mandatory.

ops-bot: Release runbook (latest): https://redwood.internal/runbooks/release-process — includes freeze checklist, PR template, and rollback playbook. :link:

raj_sre: Checklist highlights for feature release:
- release notes + owner assigned
- canary traffic plan + ramp schedule
- rollback plan + revert steps documented
- perf smoke (representative payloads) passed
- regression smoke green
- oncall pager/canary_owner assigned and announced

noah_pm: if a flaky test shows up after canary starts, what's the play?

tara_eng: If a flaky test affects release signals: pause promotion, consider rollback, quarantine test in CI, open a P1 ticket, and triage within 4-6h. If signal ambiguity persists, default to rollback.

raj_sre: Practical PR snippet we recommend adding to rollout PR body:

```
canary_owner: @username
canary_start_utc: 2026-07-15 18:00 UTC
traffic_plan: 5% -> 25% -> 50% over 24h (adjust per runbook)
rollback_steps: revert PR + disable traffic routing
sla_routes: [customer/dedicated/*]
smoke_ci_job: <CI job URL>
known_issues: [list]
```

elaine_cto: SLA note: for Dedicated customers we target <10% P99 regression on SLA routes post-release. Legal/ops working on contract language; engineering should treat SLA routes as high-sensitivity for canaries.

noah_pm: thanks — i'll put a short summary in the all-hands notes and link the PR snippet. planning a 20min office hour tomorrow 11am PT for teams with upcoming releases.

devrel: I'll add the snippet to the PR template and ping teams.

ops-bot: Reminder: next oncall rotation starts 1945040000.

noah_pm: closing this thread after the office hour doc lands. thanks everyone!
